_purpose: Read/write classification for every registered MCP tool, per action. The approval gate asks one question -- 'does this call mutate anything?' -- and this ledger is the only place that answers it. Address, classification and evidence live on the same row on purpose: when they were kept apart, the two copies drifted and nobody noticed.

_policy._why: Fail-closed. A tool or action missing from this ledger is treated as a mutation, so an upstream addition surfaces an approval card instead of silently bypassing the gate. The divergence test turns that surprise into a red build rather than a production hole.

_classification_rule: 'read' means the call leaves no persistent trace: no asset, no file on disk, no scene/component state, no Editor state a later call could observe. Anything else is 'write', including calls that only touch ephemeral Editor state -- the gate can relax those later, but it cannot un-write a file.
_shared_wrapper_note: Do not reclassify every tool as write because of the telemetry wrapper. register_all_tools (services/tools/__init__.py:63) wraps ALL 45 tools with log_execution and telemetry_tool, and the lazy TelemetryCollector creates the UnityMCP data directory and writes customer_uuid.txt on the first tool call -- even with telemetry disabled. Found and reproduced by an audit red team 2026-07-29 via manage_script_capabilities. It is deliberately NOT a classification finding: the wrapper runs identically on every call, so the first APPROVED call writes the same file, and moving reads to write buys nothing while emptying this ledger of its purpose. The classification rule above scopes to a tool's own semantics, not to infrastructure shared by all of them. The underlying defect -- an identity file created while telemetry is off -- is real, belongs to the vendored fork (untouched by us since the import commit), and is recorded as a backlog item, not fixed here.
_preflight_refresh_note: Eight tools call preflight(refresh_if_dirty=True), which -- when the Editor reports assets.external_changes_dirty -- runs refresh_unity(mode=if_dirty, scope=all, compile=request): asset import, script compilation and possibly a domain reload. That happens BEFORE the tool's own work, so it applies to the tool's read actions too. Found by an audit red team 2026-07-29 and reproduced. Every action on those eight tools is therefore classified write, marked with "preflight_refresh": true, even where the action's own semantics are a pure read. Do not 'correct' those rows back to read without first removing the refresh. The tools: find_gameobjects, manage_asset, manage_prefabs, manage_scene, manage_components, manage_gameobject, manage_texture, run_tests. Known cost, accepted by the user 2026-07-29: discovery calls such as manage_scene get_hierarchy now raise an approval card in step mode. The user's words were that the read must keep working correctly but must come with a card. A smarter future option, not built: the refresh only fires when the project is externally dirty, which is runtime state a static classifier cannot see -- a gate that could ask the server for that state could card only when the refresh would actually happen.

batch_execute.note: Carries arbitrary sub-tool calls in 'commands'. A gate that only reads the outer tool name would let every mutation through in one packet. classify() must recurse: the batch is 'read' only when every inner call is 'read'.

debug_request_context.note: Never reaches Unity; returns FastMCP request context and hub state. readOnlyHint=True.

execute_code.note: execute/replay compile and run arbitrary C# inside the Editor -- unbounded write. clear_history destroys a persisted record. The safety_checks parameter is NOT a gate: the model can set it false, and replay inherits the historical value without re-sending it.

execute_custom_tool.note: Runs a user-defined, project-scoped tool. Behaviour is not knowable statically, so it can never be classified read.

execute_menu_item.note: Calls EditorApplication.ExecuteMenuItem with any path. Only 'File/Quit' is blacklisted; Save, Build and Delete are all reachable.

find_gameobjects.note: Semantically a pure scene search -- search_method/match_mode are modifiers, not actions. Classified write anyway because find_gameobjects.py:95 calls preflight(refresh_if_dirty=True) before searching; see _preflight_refresh_note. This entry originally said read with the refresh mentioned only as a caveat, which is exactly how a known side effect becomes an unguarded one.

find_in_file.note: Sends a fixed {'action': 'read'} to manage_script and matches the regex in Python. readOnlyHint=True.

manage_animation.note: action is free-text in Python but validated against ANIMATOR_ACTIONS/CONTROLLER_ACTIONS/CLIP_ACTIONS (manage_animation.py:11-32), cross-checked against the C# switch at ManageAnimation.cs:202-249. animator_play/set_* change runtime Animator state -- no asset written, still a write.

manage_asset.note: 'import' is a write because it (re)imports into the AssetDatabase. search/get_info/get_components are semantically reads but are classified write because manage_asset.py:58 calls preflight(refresh_if_dirty=True); see _preflight_refresh_note.

param_dependent.note: Without target it reports the active platform; with target it calls SwitchActiveBuildTarget and reimports assets.
Without value it reads a PlayerSettings property; with value it writes one.
Without scenes it reads EditorBuildSettings.scenes; with scenes it replaces the whole build scene list.
Listing profiles or reading one is a read; activate=true calls SetActiveBuildProfile.

manage_build.note: The worst case for an action-only gate: four actions flip between read and write on a SIBLING parameter, not on the action name. Any gate that stops at action granularity misclassifies all four.

manage_camera.note: screenshot/screenshot_multiview always write a PNG to disk (ManageScene.cs:1249, default Assets/Screenshots), even with include_image=true. 'Taking a screenshot is harmless' is the wrong intuition here.

manage_components.note: No read path exists; the description points readers at resources instead. Also calls preflight(refresh_if_dirty=True); already all-write, but the marker records that a future read action here would still be a write. See _preflight_refresh_note.

manage_editor.note: telemetry_* short-circuit in Python and never reach Unity, and were classified read for that reason. An audit red team disproved it on 2026-07-29: manage_editor.py:33 reaches is_telemetry_enabled(), which lazily constructs TelemetryCollector, which creates the per-user UnityMCP app-data directory and writes customer_uuid.txt on a fresh profile - even with telemetry disabled. That is a persistent file on disk, so the classification rule at the top of this ledger makes it a write. Carding a status query costs almost nothing; bending the rule for one convenient case costs the rule. sync_csproj writes .sln/.csproj to disk; deploy_package/restore_package copy a package folder and trigger a recompile.

manage_fbx.note: The three writes change ModelImporter settings and reimport; full_setup also creates a .controller asset and can add a GameObject to the scene.

manage_gameobject.note: look_at writes rotation and move_relative writes position -- both are mutations despite the passive-sounding names. Also calls preflight(refresh_if_dirty=True); already all-write, but the marker records that a future read action here would still be a write. See _preflight_refresh_note.

manage_graphics.note: bake_cancel leaves partial lightmap data and bake_clear deletes baked lightmaps -- both writes despite reading like control verbs.

manage_input.note: Sends synthesized input into a running play mode session. Every acting verb is a write: it mutates live game state, and ui_click invokes arbitrary onClick handlers, so its blast radius is whatever the game's UI does. reset is a write because it removes virtual devices and clears held keys. describe is the only read -- it reports resolution status, held keys and the project's Active Input Handling setting, and is the diagnostic the model is told to call first, so carding it would tax the recovery path.

manage_material.note: Literal is authoritative and the tool description states the same split independently.

manage_physics.note: 'validate' was first classified write out of caution, then measured directly: PhysicsValidationOps.cs (308 lines) contains no SetDirty, ApplyModifiedProperties, SerializedObject or assignment-based mutation -- it is a pure report. simulate_step IS a write: Physics.Simulate moves scene transforms.

manage_prefabs.note: close_prefab_stage takes save_before_close but is a write either way -- false discards in-stage edits. open/close change which object the rest of the toolchain operates on, so they are not neutral.

manage_probuilder.note: Two Python groupings are misleading and were overridden by reading the C#: convert_to_probuilder sits in QUERY_ACTIONS but mutates the mesh (write), and select_faces only computes face indices (read). validate_mesh was measured at ProBuilderMeshUtils.cs:98 -- it counts degenerate triangles and unused vertices via reflection and writes nothing, so it is a read despite sitting next to repair_mesh.

manage_profiler.note: memory_take_snapshot writes a .snap file to disk. The profiler/frame-debugger toggles touch Editor state only, but they are observable across calls, so the conservative rule applies.

manage_scene.note: 'load' is a write because it can replace or discard current scene contents. The get_* actions and scene_view_frame are semantically reads, and validate is a pure report unless auto_repair is set (ManageScene.cs:298) -- all of them are classified write anyway because manage_scene.py:90 calls preflight(refresh_if_dirty=True); see _preflight_refresh_note. That also retires the auto_repair param_dependent rule: the action is a write either way now. NOTE for anyone reading the old Backend exemption list: manage_scene has no 'get_info' action -- that entry never matched anything, confirmed against the live server on 2026-07-29.

manage_scriptable_object.note: The C# handler may accept more actions than the Python Literal exposes, but only the Python surface is reachable through this tool.

manage_sprite.note: full_setup is a composite (vision -> slice -> clips -> controller) and writes at every stage.

manage_texture.note: No read action exists on this tool. Also calls preflight(refresh_if_dirty=True); already all-write, but the marker records that a future read action here would still be a write. See _preflight_refresh_note.

manage_tools.note: Server-only meta-tool: no Unity command is sent. activate/deactivate/reset change nothing and return an error pointing at the profile URLs (tool lists are fixed per URL, not per session); list_groups reads server state; sync only READS the get_tool_states resource and updates the server-level group state. Classified read despite readOnlyHint=False. A group becoming visible is not a gate bypass -- the tools it exposes are still classified individually on their own calls.

manage_ui.note: render_ui is a write on two counts: File.WriteAllBytes of a PNG (ManageUI.cs:914, :1154) and assigning a RenderTexture to the PanelSettings asset (:1170). link_stylesheet edits the UXML file.

manage_vfx.note: Playback controls mutate live component state rather than a serialized asset; the C# layout corroborates the split with explicit *Read.cs vs *Write.cs/*Control.cs pairs.

apply_text_edits.note: Writes .cs content under Assets/ and can trigger a recompile via wait_for_compile.

validate_script.note: readOnlyHint=True. 'level' is a validation depth, not an action.

manage_script.note: Tool-level annotation is destructiveHint=True with no readOnlyHint, so the read action is under-declared at tool level -- per-action gating is required to avoid carding every script read.

manage_script_capabilities.note: unity_target=None -- returns a static capability dict from the Python server, never reaches Unity.

get_sha.note: readOnlyHint=True. Returns sha256 and length only, not contents.

read_console.note: 'clear' invokes LogEntries.Clear (ReadConsole.cs:205). It destroys ephemeral UI state, not project data, but it is still destructive and must not ride on a blanket tool-level exemption. Defaults to 'get' when action is omitted (read_console.py:52) -- classify() must apply that default rather than treating a missing action as unknown.

refresh_unity.note: mode/scope/compile are modifiers, not actions. Imports assets and regenerates artifacts even with compile='none'.

run_tests.note: 'mode' is EditMode/PlayMode, not an action. Executes arbitrary project code inside the Editor; PlayMode forces a domain reload. Also calls preflight(refresh_if_dirty=True); already all-write, but the marker records that a future read action here would still be a write. See _preflight_refresh_note.

get_test_job.note: readOnlyHint=True. Polls an already-started job; starts nothing.

script_apply_edits.note: The per-edit 'op' field selects the structured edit; every op is a mutation.

set_active_instance.note: unity_target=None -- the Unity project is never touched; it only discovers instances and resolves the identifier. It no longer stores a selection (routing is per call: unity_instance argument, ?instance= / X-Unity-Instance on the connection, or the sole instance), so it cannot redirect later writes; it always answers success=false with the resolved Name@hash and how to route to it.

unity_docs.note: readOnlyHint=True, destructiveHint=False. action is free-text but whitelisted against ALL_ACTIONS (unity_docs.py:13, enforced at :736). All four fetch remote docs over HTTP from docs.unity3d.com -- read with respect to Unity, but note they do reach the network.

unity_reflect.note: readOnlyHint=True, destructiveHint=False. Free-text action validated against ALL_ACTIONS (unity_reflect.py:11); confirmed against the C# switch at UnityReflect.cs:118. Pure reflection over loaded assemblies.

game_hooks.note: Playtest group (P4 contract). list enumerates hooks the game opted into; get evaluates state hooks (static properties/fields or GameHooks.State getters) and serialises their values -- no asset, file or scene write. call invokes an action hook, which is arbitrary game code (level.restart, input.jump), so it is a write. Caveat accepted by the contract: a state getter is game code too, and a getter with side effects would run uncarded; the game owns its hooks.

play_session.note: start can load a scene, enters play mode (domain reload), changes Time.captureDeltaTime/fixedDeltaTime, runInBackground and InputSettings in memory, adds virtual input devices and calls hook level.restart. stop restores all of that and exits play. status only reports playing/paused/frame/time.

play_step.note: Advances the game by N frames with injected input and optional autopilot hook calls -- mutates live game state; captures write PNGs under Library/GamachineCaptures/.

play_capture.note: Writes a full-resolution PNG under <project>/Library/GamachineCaptures/ on every call (same reasoning as manage_camera screenshot: a file on disk is a write even though the call looks passive).

run_playtest.note: start runs whole scenarios: scene loads, play mode enter/exit, hook calls, input, captures on disk. Defaults to start when action is omitted (run_playtest.py, RunPlaytestTool.cs). status only reads the last job's progress/results (RunPlaytestTool.Status -> PlaytestRunner.StatusData builds a JObject from the job fields; the server forwards only {action: status}) -- read by owner decision 25 Sep 2026.
